The cabin was small, crooked, and smelled faintly of pine, smoke, and whatever mysterious thing had died beneath the floorboards last winter.
I had grown rather fond of it.
Far beyond the nearest village, tucked between the Whispering Woods and a mountain that occasionally sneezed sparks, it was the perfect place to avoid taxes, adventurers, and other people's problems.
I was halfway through burning a particularly disappointing stew when someone knocked on my door.
Three knocks.
Polite ones.
That was suspicious.
I opened it and found myself staring at a very tall fellow with the body of a man and the head, wings, and legs of a stork. He wore a little blue courier's cap and carried a sealed letter in his beak.
"Delivery," he announced.
I blinked.
"You're a stork."
"Half stork."
"Right. Important distinction."
He handed me the letter.
The seal bore a familiar emblem: a crooked purple star surrounded by tiny flames.
"Oh no," I muttered.
The Misfortunate Blorbo Bleebus.
My oldest friend, professional disaster, and the only goblin I knew who had once accidentally cursed himself.

I broke the seal.

I stared at the letter.
Then at the stork-man.
"Does he pay you extra for delivering messages like this?"
"No."
"Shame."
The courier turned to leave.
"Wait," I said. "One question."
He looked back.
"So, uh... since you're a stork, do you deliver children too?"
There was a long silence.
The courier slowly lowered his wing.
"Only messages."
"Right."
"Children are handled by a completely different department."
"Ah."
He stared at me.
I stared at him.
"...Good to know," I said.
He shook his head, muttered something about "forest weirdos," and flew away.
I looked back at my cabin.
Then at Blorbo's letter.
